carl: Heads up — noticed a p95/p99 jump for short‑seq (<=64) requests across the low‑latency pool starting ~08:05 UTC after last night's infra roll. ~40–60% latency increase. Any ideas?

nina: I can repro on canary. Traces show the attention op picking a different kernel path for short sequences — it used to pick attn-fast-v1, now it's picking attn-fused-v3. Latency delta visible at first token.

ben: Pinned a single request and profiled. Kernel selection log from runtime: 
```
[2026-03-18T08:06:12Z] kernel_selector: model=redwood-7b, op=attention, seq_len=32, chosen=attn_fused_v3, workspace=1.18GB, est_latency=0.72ms
[2026-03-18T08:06:12Z] fallback_candidates: attn_fast_v1(est=0.42ms), cudnn_attn(est=0.9ms)
```
So heuristics are preferring the fused variant now.

ryan: We rolled driver 535.8 -> 536.1 last night on the canary nodes as part of the NV driver rollout. There was a small ABI change in the driver that adjusts available workspace reporting to CUDA. Could affect kernel workspace heuristics.

ops-bot: @deploy-bot posted: "driver-update: nv-driver-536.1 roll to canary at 2026-03-18T03:10:00Z" :information_source:

sre-janet: I looked at host telemetry for the affected hosts — PCIe replays and mem_ctrl stalls spike concurrently with the latency events on noisy-tenant VMs. Could be contention + kernel workspace interaction causing thrashing.

nina: Interesting. The runtime kernel selector multiplies estimated workspace by a heuristic that used to be driver-reported. If driver is reporting slightly larger workspace available, selector may prefer the fused kernel which has higher startup cost but lower amortized per‑token cost — bad for short sequences.

ben: Quick experiment: forced runtime override to prefer attn_fast_v1 for seq<=64. Patch applied to a single canary shard. Results: median similar, p95 reverted to baseline (~40% lower than fused choice), throughput same.

ben: Test numbers (canary shard): 
```
before (fused_v3): p50=12ms p95=68ms p99=140ms
after (force fast_v1): p50=11.5ms p95=38ms p99=80ms
```

carl: Nice. Can we roll this as a hotfix for the low‑latency pool while we investigate driver/heuristic interaction?

ryan: I can coordinate a rollback of driver to 535.8 on a small subset, but that's higher blast radius. Safer: apply runtime selector hotfix that biases for small seq lengths and GPU memory headroom.

nina: I'll open a PR with a tuned selector: prefer low‑startup kernels when seq<=64 or if active_kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.8. Also add telemetry hooks to log chosen kernels + driver workspace reported so we can correlate.

ops-bot: @carl created issue REDWOOD‑INF‑4891: "short‑seq latency regression — kernel selector change after driver roll" :page_facing_up:

sre-janet: After the override rollout p95 on prod low‑latency pool dropped back to expected. We'll keep noisy-tenant isolation plan in place and watch PCIe stall counters.

carl: OK let's do hotfix rollout to all low‑latency shards, keep driver rollback as contingency. Add a postmortem note and schedule deeper investigation on driver workspace reporting and selector thresholds. Thanks all :thumbsup:
